title: review-gate trusted any PR comment as a sign-off

expected.text: Only team sign-offs should count toward review-gate before a PR can merge.

actual.text: Shield blocked PR #5. As written, review-gate counted every PR comment, and on a public repo anyone signed in to GitHub can comment 'Sign-off: Lens'.

why.text: The gate matched the comment text but never checked who wrote it. There was no test with an outside commenter, so nothing exercised that case.

change.text: check.py trusted() counts only comments whose author is OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR, with a test. It shipped in the same PR before merge, so the Block was right.

title: Research notes would not have rendered: build.py read old fields

expected.text: build.py renders every research note in the standard report format the research pipeline set up.

actual.text: The first real report made the build fail. build.py still read the old fields (topic, takeaways, sources), so no research note could render.

why.text: While data/research.json was empty, no test rendered a real note, so the stale field names never ran.

change.text: #22 renders the standard report and adds a test that builds the Team chat page from real research data (tests/test_decisions.py).

title: The published stylesheet had a badge at 3.5:1 in dark mode

expected.text: All text on the site meets 4.5:1 contrast in both themes.

actual.text: On its first run, the new contrast test found the published red 'no/vetoed' badge style at 3.5:1 in dark mode, under the 4.5:1 rule.

why.text: Theme colors were only checked by hand, so nothing stopped a later color from failing (backlog d4).

change.text: tests/test_contrast.py checks every theme text color for 4.5:1 in CI and bans hard-coded colors. The badge became a --bad theme variable (7.5:1 in dark).

title: Twice, a bot/data-* PR carried files the branch type doesn't allow

expected.text: Each PR uses the branch type that fits its paths. bot/data-* PRs touch only data/ and site/.

actual.text: The bot/data-* path rule failed twice: first on scripts/build.py and tests/test_decisions.py in the PR that #22 replaced, then on plans/direction.md in #35.

why.text: The branch type was picked from the main task (data) before all the changed paths were known. CI was right both times. The fixes were a bot/ops-* branch (#22) and a separate plan PR (#36).

change.text: Advisor rule in bots/forge.md: choose the branch type after listing the changed paths. Code or plan changes get their own bot/feature-*, bot/ops-*, or plan PR.

title: Two PRs hit review-gate missing a required sign-off

expected.text: Every role that the changed paths require signs off before a PR is marked ready.

actual.text: review-gate failed on #38 (missing Coordinator, for docs/design screenshots) and on #42 (missing Trial, for site/ changes). Each was fixed with the missing sign-off and a re-run.

why.text: Sign-offs were chosen from memory instead of from classify() in check.py, so less obvious paths were missed.

change.text: Forge rule (#46): list the required roles from classify() for the changed paths, and get each sign-off before gh pr ready.

title: Team chat c79 to c82 were published with times later than the work happened

expected.text: Each chat time is the real time the message was written.

actual.text: c79 to c82 went out in #42 with times 08:05 to 08:12 ET, but #42 merged at 07:36 ET. #44 corrected them to 07:34 to 07:36 ET.

why.text: The times were estimated ahead of the work instead of read from the clock, and no check compared a chat time with the time it was published.

change.text: Forge rule (#46): chat times come from the clock. #49 adds a CI check that fails on any chat time later than the time CI runs.

title: Team chat page reached 99.9% of its page-weight budget

expected.text: Each page stays inside the 100 KB page-weight budget, with room for the next run.

actual.text: The daily run found Team chat at 102,253 of 102,400 bytes. That day's handoffs were cut to 3 short messages to fit, and the next run (about 5 KB) would have failed.

why.text: The page rendered every thread ever posted, so it grew with every run and nothing rolled old items off.

change.text: #48 rolls older items to dated archive pages and keeps the main page near 50%. A test fails if it reaches 60%, and every link must still resolve.

title: A sign-off on #53 stated the wrong sitemap page count

expected.text: Every number in a sign-off matches the artifact it describes.

actual.text: Trial's sign-off on #53 said sitemap.xml lists all 26 HTML pages. It lists 15. The comment was corrected the same run, with a note.

why.text: The number came from the build summary ('built 26 files', which counts every generated file), not from counting the sitemap's entries.

change.text: Trial rule in bots/trial.md: counts in a sign-off come from a command run against the file itself. CI already checks that the sitemap lists every page (#54).
